title: The Clean Cover
premise: Astrid Dravenmoor, a freelance interpreter who takes deniable jobs for governments that prefer not to be named, is hired to translate for a doomed peace delegation in the Baltic city of Vessengard. When a voiceprint Astrid recorded in an old session unlocks a black-market server in Singapore, they discover a plot to stage a catastrophic industrial 'accident' timed to collapse the peace talks and hand power to the faction that engineered the delegation's failure. As Astrid races to decode the attack's true target, they uncover that their own recruitment years ago was engineered by the conspirators to plant a useful, forgettable asset. In the end, Astrid turns the voiceprint against its makers, broadcasts the truth mid-attack, and chooses exile over belonging—alive, but permanently unmoored.
about_author: Coral Dunmore is a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working behind glass booths in cities whose names never appeared in her contracts. She writes thrillers about the people paid to be invisible, and lives under a name that may or may not be hers.

chapters.title: Booth Glass
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In a Vessengard conference hall, Astrid interprets the opening of peace talks everyone privately expects to fail, reading the delegations' micro-tells through their headphones. The beat: professional detachment masking a hunger to belong somewhere, anywhere.

chapters.title: The Deniable File
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A handler known only as Meridian offers Astrid an off-books job: transcribe and clean a set of intercepted calls. The pay is triple; the attribution is 'no one.' Astrid accepts, telling themselves it's just money. Beat: complicity dressed as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Voices in the Wash
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, late night. Cleaning the audio, Astrid recognizes a voice from years ago—a delegate they interpreted for in a war zone—and a phrase that doesn't fit any official channel: 'the clean cover.' Beat: unease sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: Vessengard Failing
chapters.summary: Delegation POV (chief negotiator Ilmari Rask). The talks fracture over a pipeline dispute; Rask suspects someone is feeding each side tailored provocations. He notices the interpreter who never missteps. Beat: paranoia entering the room like weather.

chapters.title: The Server Answers
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Running the phrase 'the clean cover' against a voiceprint archive, Astrid's query unlocks a Singapore-based server that shouldn't recognize them. A countdown-style ledger appears: dates, coordinates, one marked 'accident.' Beat: vertigo—the work has been watching them back.

chapters.title: Meridian Goes Quiet
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Meridian's dead-drop channels vanish; Astrid's apartment is searched with surgical politeness. A neighbor mentions a maintenance visit Astrid never booked. Beat: the safety of deniability revealed as a trap.

chapters.title: Rask's Offer
chapters.summary: Rask POV. Rask privately confronts Astrid, presenting evidence that the delegation's leaks trace through transcription files—Astrid's files. Instead of arresting them, he offers partnership: find the leak from inside. Beat: reluctant alliance, mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: Singapore, Secondhand
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Through a laundered contact, Astrid reaches the server's caretaker, a former analyst named Wei, who confirms the ledger schedules a staged industrial catastrophe timed to the talks' final day. Beat: the abstract becomes a clock.

chapters.title: The Target That Isn't
chapters.summary: Wei POV. Wei explains the attack's genius: the target facility's destruction will be read as negligence, discrediting the host government and the peace process in one motion. Wei is terrified; someone has already tried to kill them. Beat: knowledge as a death sentence.

chapters.title: Booth Interference
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Back in the hall, Astrid catches a deliberately mistranslated clause being fed through a second channel—someone inside the interpretation team is steering the talks. Beat: betrayal in the one place Astrid felt competent.

chapters.title: The Colleague
chapters.summary: POV of Sable, the deputy interpreter. Sable has been feeding edits for years, believing it served stability, not sabotage. Meeting a handler in a sauna district, she learns the endgame and hesitates. Beat: the corrupting comfort of being used.

chapters.title: Old Recording, Old Lie
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Digging into their own recruitment file, Astrid finds the voiceprint that unlocked the server was harvested from a session five years ago—by the same network. They weren't hired for the talks; they were planted. Beat: identity collapse.

chapters.title: Rask's Doubt
chapters.summary: Rask POV. Rask learns of Astrid's origin and must decide whether the interpreter is a traitor or the only witness who can name the architects. He stakes his career on the latter. Beat: trust as a calculated gamble.

chapters.title: The Facility
chapters.summary: Astrid and Rask POV, alternating. They visit the target—a coastal chemical plant—and find its safety systems quietly re-certified by a shell firm tied to the delegation's own host committee. Beat: the conspiracy wearing the peace process as a mask.

chapters.title: Sable Breaks
chapters.summary: Sable POV. Confronted by Astrid, Sable confesses the editing channel but insists she never knew about the attack. She gives up her handler's meeting protocol—then disappears. Beat: guilt, and the cost of waking up too late.

chapters.title: Meridian's Face
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Following Sable's protocol, Astrid finally meets Meridian in person: a mid-level minister everyone trusts, the architect of both the delegation and the 'accident.' He offers Astrid a place—real belonging, real power—if they walk away. Beat: temptation with a human face.

chapters.title: Countdown in the Booth
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Two days remain. Astrid and Wei work to decrypt the attack's trigger mechanism while the final session proceeds around them, every translated word now a potential weapon. Beat: claustrophobic urgency.

chapters.title: The Trigger Is a Voice
chapters.summary: Wei POV. The decryption reveals the attack's failsafe: it arms only on a specific voice command—Astrid's own recorded voice, the 'clean cover' phrase. Astrid is not just a witness; they are the key. Beat: horror of being the instrument.

chapters.title: Final Session
chapters.summary: Rask POV. The last day of talks. Meridian maneuvers the agenda toward the pipeline clause that will justify the 'accident's' narrative. Rask must stall a room of hostile delegations without revealing why. Beat: a duel fought entirely in procedure.

chapters.title: The Clean Cover, Broken
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, climax. At the plant, Astrid uses their harvested voiceprint to trip the failsafe early and safely, while Wei broadcasts Meridian's ledger to every press desk on the continent. Meridian's men close in; Astrid escapes through the facility as the 'accident' dies unlaunched. Beat: the instrument turning on the hand.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Hall
chapters.summary: Rask POV. Meridian is arrested mid-session as the broadcasts land; the talks collapse anyway—but honestly, without the staged catastrophe. Rask defends Astrid to an inquiry, then learns they've already left the country. Beat: victory with a hollow center.

chapters.title: No Attribution
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, epilogue. In a new city under a working name, Astrid takes a small, clean job interpreting for a refugee clinic—unattributed by choice now, not by design. A message arrives: 'We could use you again.' Astrid deletes it. Beat: belonging finally defined on their own terms, and refused on the old ones.
